title: Matching before the magnitude-gap filter allowed a reversed deep-earthquake pair majority at 300 km in ComCat, 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether the larger-first majority in deep earthquake pairs survives all largest disjoint pair sets when matching comes before the magnitude-gap filter. We reused 785 ComCat events with depth greater than 300 km and magnitude at least 5.5 in 2000-2025. The primary rule used positive lags through seven days and hypocenter distances through 200 km. Every largest matching had 81 edges before filtering; 42-57 pairs had magnitude gaps of at least 0.3. Exact bounds on the retained larger-first share were 60.4%-83.3%. At 300 km, the range was 46.4%-78.7%, whereas filtering before matching gave a lower bound of 56.1%. Thus filter order can reverse the majority claim at the wider radius. Component dynamic programming, integer-weight blossom optimization and independent exhaustive enumeration agreed. These are fixed-catalog selection bounds, not confidence limits, evidence against triggering or a forecast. The endpoint choices use order labels and need not represent a practical pairing rule. Catalog error and detection effects remain untested. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, a static figure and source provenance; external event records remain outside it.

display.caption: Exact bounds across largest disjoint pair sets. Blue lines use magnitude-gap filtering after matching. Orange endpoints use filtering before matching. The ranges measure selection sensitivity in a fixed catalog, not sampling uncertainty.
